```{r}
source("assets/setup.R")
f <- function(x, d = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d)
mat$delivery <- relevel(mat$delivery, ref = "Home")
m2 <- MASS::polr(anaemia ~ wealth + education + bmi + anc_visits + parity + age + tribal + residence, data = mat, Hess = TRUE)
mn <- nnet::multinom(delivery ~ wealth + education + anc_visits + residence + tribal, data = mat, trace = FALSE)
br <- suppressWarnings(brant(m2))
```

::: {.sheet}

## 1 · Which model?

| Outcome | Example | Model | R |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Ordered**, 3+ categories | anaemia grade, BP stage | **Ordinal logistic** (proportional odds) | `MASS::polr(y ~ x, Hess = TRUE)` |
| ... if the assumption fails for few predictors | | **Partial proportional odds** | `ordinal::clm(y ~ x, nominal = ~ z)` |
| **Nominal**, 3+ categories | place of delivery | **Multinomial logistic** | `nnet::multinom(y ~ x)` (set the **reference**) |
| Binary | any anaemia | Logistic | `glm(family = binomial)` |

Check first: **order meaningful?** **Smallest category** big enough (here `r min(table(mat$anaemia))` women)? Never code categories 1-4 for linear regression.

## 2 · Ordinal logistic

| Item | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `logit P(Y <= k) = zeta_k - x*beta` | one **threshold** per cut-point (**K - 1**), **one beta per predictor** |
| exp(beta) | **odds ratio for a higher category**, the same at every cut-point |
| polr beta > 0 | higher (worse) categories more likely |
| Our result: wealth | OR **`r f(exp(coef(m2))[["wealth"]])`** per quintile: `r f(100 * (1 - exp(coef(m2))[["wealth"]]), 0)`% lower odds of a worse category |

## 3 · Checking proportional odds

| Tool | What it shows |
|---|---|
| **`brant(model)`** | omnibus p and one p per predictor; here omnibus p = `r f(br["Omnibus", "probability"], 3)`, tribal p = `r f(br["tribalYes", "probability"], 3)`, wealth p = `r f(br["wealth", "probability"], 2)` |
| **Binary models at each cut** | `glm(I(y >= k) ~ x)` for each k: ORs should be similar |
| **LR test** `anova(clm_po, clm_partial)` | does freeing a predictor improve the fit? |
| If it fails | **partial PO** for the offending predictor, **cut-specific ORs**, or **multinomial** |

## 4 · Multinomial logistic

| Item | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **K - 1 equations** vs the **reference** | each predictor has K - 1 coefficients |
| exp(coef) | **relative risk ratio** (odds vs the reference) |
| Our result: wealth | RRR `r f(exp(coef(mn)["PHC", "wealth"]))` (PHC), `r f(exp(coef(mn)["Public hospital", "wealth"]))` (public), **`r f(exp(coef(mn)["Private hospital", "wealth"]))` (private)**, each vs Home |
| No p-values printed | z = coef / SE: `s <- summary(mn); s$coefficients / s$standard.errors` |
| A whole variable | likelihood-ratio test: `anova(model_without, model_with)` |
| Reference | changes **presentation**, not the **fit** |

## 5 · Showing results

`predict(model, newdata, type = "probs")` gives the **probability of each category** (adds to 1). Plot against a key predictor. **Do not judge by accuracy** (`r f(mean(predict(mn) == mat$delivery), 2)` here vs `r f(max(prop.table(table(mat$delivery))), 2)` for guessing).

## 6 · Pitfalls

::: {.bad}
- **Categories coded 1-4** in linear regression; **dichotomising** needlessly
- **No assumption check**; a **single OR** that hides a violation (tribal group here: OR about `r f(exp(coef(m2))[["tribalYes"]], 1)`, but about 3 for severe anaemia)
- **Sparse categories**; a multinomial model with too many parameters for the sample
- RRR read as a **risk ratio**; **accuracy** as the measure of fit
- **Association read as cause**
:::

## 7 · One-paragraph report

*Among 1,500 women, anaemia (none, mild, moderate, severe) was modelled with a proportional-odds model adjusted for education, BMI, antenatal visits, parity, age, tribal group and residence. Each higher wealth quintile was associated with `r f(100 * (1 - exp(coef(m2))[["wealth"]]), 0)`% lower odds of a worse category (OR `r f(exp(coef(m2))[["wealth"]])`). The Brant test rejected proportional odds for tribal group only (p < 0.001), whose effect was concentrated on severe anaemia, so it is reported by cut-point. Place of delivery was modelled with a multinomial logit (reference: home): each wealth quintile multiplied the relative risk of private-hospital delivery `r f(exp(coef(mn)["Private hospital", "wealth"]), 1)`-fold.*

:::
